summary: Wall-clock thresholds (values unchanged) are judged only with PANTHEON_SOURCE_INGEST_WALL_CLOCK_BOUNDS=1; the default required check asserts counters that do not depend on host speed and proves with three injected faults that those counters catch what the bounds were for. No production code changed.
honest_gaps: AC1 sample sizes: 9 'idle' and 4 loaded baseline runs (not 30/30). One run of this test is 45 s idle and ~95 s loaded; foreground batches are capped at 10 min. The host is a shared 12-core machine (load average ~5 from other workers) so 'idle' is 'shared-host baseline'.

AC1 harness caveat: baseline runs use a harness that builds the hosted-shaped fixture once and runs the test function on a fresh copy of the seeded sqlite file each run. Its reader_process values (median 140 ms) are higher than the same test under pytest (5-46 ms), so the reader_process failure counts below overstate; write txn p99 and maintenance step are not affected by that difference.

AC2/3: test_retention.py (needs pyarrow) and test_evidence_read_cost.py (needs real PostgreSQL) are skipped on this host so their maxima could not be measured; they are gated by the class rule (same fsync/DB-wait class, bounds 250/100 ms and 0.5 s) and listed as 'not measured'.
AC2 inventory maxima for the 4 fast files come from 17-18 runs under load (30 s per run), not 30.

AC6: the opt-in path did NOT pass on this host in 2 of 2 runs (write txn p99 287.9 ms and 279.0 ms vs 250 ms; every other bound passed). The same single slow fsync class as the CI failure; the bound is not raised. The opt-in command itself works and printed the values below.
AC6 default path: 203 clean runs (50 + 3x34 + 3x17, run in separate processes in series/parallel under load) with 0 failures; not a single uninterrupted 200-run process.
